title: Optimal Training-Time Scaling in Gradual Adaptation
abstract: arXiv:2608.04927v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: In gradual adaptation, how should the training time on each task change as the number of intermediate tasks increases? We study this question for overparameterized linear regression tasks that change smoothly and share a zero-loss solution. With $N$ tasks and training time $s_N$ on each, the final learning progress converges to a continuum curve when $Ns_N\to\tau$. The limiting progress is $\Theta(\tau)$ for small $\tau$ and $\Theta(\tau^{-1})$ for large $\tau$, so both very short and very long training produce little progress. It follows that optimal per-task training times scale as $s_N^\star=\Theta(N^{-1})$, equivalently $Ns_N^\star=\Theta(1)$. Experiments on gradually rotated MNIST and a natural Yearbook time shift are consistent with less per-task training as the path is divided more finely.

translated_title: 渐进适应中的最优训练时间缩放
translated_abstract: 在渐进适应中，随着中间任务数量的增加，每个任务上的训练时间应如何变化？我们针对平滑变化且共享零损失解的过参数化线性回归任务研究了这一问题。设有 $N$ 个任务、每个任务训练时间为 $s_N$，当 $Ns_N\to\tau$ 时，最终学习进度收敛到一条连续统曲线。当 $\tau$ 较小时，极限进度为 $\Theta(\tau)$；当 $\tau$ 较大时，极限进度为 $\Theta(\tau^{-1})$，因此过短和过长的训练都只能带来很小的进度。由此可知，最优的每任务训练时间按 $s_N^\star=\Theta(N^{-1})$ 缩放，等价于 $Ns_N^\star=\Theta(1)$。在渐进旋转的 MNIST 和自然的 Yearbook 时间偏移数据上的实验均与“任务路径划分越细、每任务所需训练越少”的结论一致。
tldr: 该论文证明了在渐进适应中，最优的每任务训练时间应随中间任务数量按 $1/N$ 缩放（即总训练量保持常数），因为过短或过长的训练都会使最终学习进度趋于零。
en_tdlr: The paper proves that in gradual adaptation the optimal per-task training time should scale as $\Theta(1/N)$ with the number of intermediate tasks (i.e., constant total training budget), since both too short and too long training yield vanishing final learning progress.
